references.text: The fulfillment of the promise that the Lord would come down on Mount Sinai on the third day, with thunder, lightning, and a thick cloud.
The Lord comes down in a cloud on Mount Sinai, a parallel to his visible presence among the people.
Moses' blessing recalls how the Lord came from Sinai and appeared before his people.
The third day as a significant moment for divine action, when Abraham saw the place of the sacrifice.
Preparation for three days before a great divine act, when Israel was to cross the Jordan.
The third day as the time for the Lord's restorative action, a prophetic parallel.
Christ was raised on the third day, fulfilling the pattern of the third day as a moment of divine revelation.
Hebrews refers to the theophany at Sinai as an image of God's presence and holiness.
Both verses emphasize the need to be ready before God's revelation on Mount Sinai.
